questions.question: Beriberi is caused by deficiency of which of the following?
questions.questionHtml: Beriberi is caused by deficiency of which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Vitamin B1.
Key Points
  • Beriberi is caused by a deficiency of Vitamin B1 or thiamine.
  • Thiamine is essential for energy metabolism and nerve function, and its deficiency can lead to various symptoms including fatigue, muscle weakness, and nerve damage.
  • Beriberi is a disease caused by prolonged thiamine deficiency, and its symptoms include muscle wasting, nerve damage, and heart failure.
Additional Information
  • Vitamin D deficiency can lead to various bone disorders, but it is not directly related to Beriberi.
  • Vitamin C deficiency can lead to scurvy, which is characterized by bleeding gums and skin lesions, but it is also not related to Beriberi.
  • Iodine deficiency can lead to goiter and thyroid disorders, but it is not related to Beriberi.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of Mass Media?

questions.question: Which famous experiment was done by Michael Faraday in 1831?
questions.questionHtml: Which famous experiment was done by Michael Faraday in 1831?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Discovery of electromagnetic induction.

Key Points

  • Michael Faraday, an English scientist, conducted the famous experiment in 1831 which led to the discovery of electromagnetic induction.
  • Electromagnetic induction is the process of generating an electromotive force (EMF) through the relative motion between a conductor and a magnetic field.
  • This discovery paved the way for numerous technological advancements, including the development of electric generators and transformers.
  • Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction states that the induced EMF in any closed circuit is equal to the rate of change of the magnetic flux through the circuit.

Additional Information

  • Electromagnetic Induction
    • Electromagnetic induction refers to the generation of an electric current by changing the magnetic field. This phenomenon is fundamental to many types of electrical devices, including generators and transformers.
    • Faraday's Experiment: In 1831, Faraday discovered that when a magnet is moved in and out of a coil of wire, an electric current is induced in the wire. This is known as Faraday's law of induction.
    • Lenz's Law: This law states that the direction of the induced current is such that it opposes the change in magnetic flux that caused it. This is a consequence of the law of conservation of energy.
    • Applications: The principles of electromagnetic induction are applied in many devices, such as inductors, transformers, and many types of electrical generators.
  • Quantum Magnetometers
    • Quantum magnetometers are devices that measure magnetic fields using quantum effects. These are used in various applications, including medical imaging and geological surveys.
  • Law of Elasticity
    • The law of elasticity, also known as Hooke's Law, states that the deformation of a material is directly proportional to the force applied to it, provided the material's elastic limit is not exceeded.
  • Natural Radioactivity
    • Natural radioactivity refers to the spontaneous decay of unstable atomic nuclei, resulting in the emission of radiation. This phenomenon was discovered by Henri Becquerel in 1896.

questions.question: Who among the following discovered laws of planetary motion?

questions.solution:
Kepler's three laws of planetary motion can be described as follows:

The path of the planets about the sun is elliptical in shape, with the center of the sun being located at one focus. (The Law of Ellipses)

An imaginary line drawn from the center of the sun to the center of the planet will sweep out equal areas in equal intervals of time. (The Law of Equal Areas)

The ratio of the squares of the periods of any two planets is equal to the ratio of the cubes of their average distances from the sun. (The Law of Harmonies)

questions.question: The substances which reduce friction are called _______.
questions.questionHtml: The substances which reduce friction are called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lubricants.

Key Points

  • Lubricants:-
    • These are substances that are introduced between two surfaces in contact in order to reduce friction. (Hence option 4 is correct)
    • They do this by forming a thin layer between the surfaces, which prevents them from rubbing directly against each other.
    • This reduces the amount of heat generated and the wear and tear on the surfaces. 
    • There are many different types of lubricants, including:
      • Oils
      • Greases
      • Solids, such as graphite and molybdenum disulfide
      • Liquids, such as water and silicone
      • Gases, such as air and nitrogen

Additional Information

  • Fluids:-
    • These are substances that can flow easily and continuously deform under an applied shear stress, or external force.
    • They have zero shear modulus, or, in simpler terms, are substances which cannot resist any shear force applied to them.
  • Magnet:-
    • It is a material or object that produces a magnetic field.
    • This magnetic field is invisible but is responsible for the most notable property of a magnet: a force that pulls on other ferromagnetic materials, such as iron, steel, nickel, cobalt, etc. and attracts or repels other magnets.
  • Spring:-
    • It is an elastic object that stores mechanical energy and releases it when the opposing force is removed.
    • Springs can be made from a variety of materials, including metal, plastic, and rubber.
    • They come in all shapes and sizes, and can be used in a wide variety of applications.

questions.question: In biology, the term "IVF" stands for __________.
questions.questionHtml: In biology, the term "IVF" stands for __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is In vitro fertilization. 

Key Points

  • In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) is a type of assisted reproductive technology (ART) used to help individuals or couples conceive a child.
  • The term "in vitro" is a Latin term meaning "in glass," referring to the test tubes used in laboratories, although the actual process now uses more advanced technology.

Additional Information

  • Here is a basic outline of the IVF process:
  • Ovarian stimulation and monitoring:
    • The woman is given hormonal medications to stimulate the ovaries to produce multiple eggs instead of the single egg typically released during a menstrual cycle.
    • Regular ultrasound and blood tests are performed to monitor the development of the follicles (fluid-filled ovarian sacs that contain the eggs).
  • Egg retrieval:
    • Once the eggs mature, a medical procedure known as follicular aspiration is performed to retrieve them.
    • A thin needle is inserted through the vagina and into the ovary under ultrasound guidance, and the fluid in the follicles is aspirated.
  • Insemination and Fertilization:
    • The eggs are combined with sperm in a petri dish and incubated overnight. If traditional IVF doesn't seem promising, a single sperm may be injected directly into an egg, a process known as intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI).
  • Embryo culture:
    • The fertilized eggs (now embryos) are monitored for growth.
    • The goal is to grow these embryos for about five days until they reach a stage called the blastocyst stage.
  • Embryo transfer:
    • Once the embryos are ready, one or more are transferred into the woman's uterus through the cervix using a thin catheter.
    • If an embryo implants in the lining of the uterus and grows, a pregnancy results.

  • The input for ALU includes the operand(data on which the operation is to be performed) and the code which indicates which operation has to be performed on the given data.
  • Based on the input, the ALU performs the operation on binary numbers.

questions.question: Who invented the capillary feed fountainpen?
questions.questionHtml: Who invented the capillary feed fountainpen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​LE Waterman.

Key Points

  • ​Lewis Waterman invented a superior fountain pen that made inkwells and dip pens obsolete.
  • It is a writing instrument equipped with a metal nib (usually solid gold) that utilizes a cartridge for the flow of ink.

Additional Information

  • David Hughes was a British-American inventor, practical experimenter, and professor of music known for his work on the printing telegraph and the microphone.
  • Ian Donald, a Scottish physician pioneered the use of diagnostic ultrasound.
  • Alfred Nobel born in Stockholm invented Dynamite in 1866.

questions.question: Who invented the lightning conductor?
questions.questionHtml: Who invented the lightning conductor?
questions.solution:
• A lightning rod or lightning conductor invented by Benjamin Franklin in 1752 in Pennsylvania in 1749, is a metal rod mounted on a structure and intended to protect the structure from a lightning strike.
  • If lightning hits the structure, it will preferentially strike the rod and be conducted to ground through a wire, instead of passing through the structure, where it could start a fire or cause electrocution. Lightning rods are also called finials, air terminals or strike termination devices.

questions.question: _______ is a mode of communication in itself, and it also regulates the use of other means of communication.
questions.questionHtml: _______ is a mode of communication in itself, and it also regulates the use of other means of communication.
questions.solution: A satellite is an artificial object placed into orbit for various purposes such as communication, remote sensing, weather forecasting, and research. Satellites facilitate the transmission of radio, television, and telephone signals worldwide.
